# Controlled development fixture admission

These 45 locally generated byte sequences are the only input admitted by the
current development PDF policy. The checked-in digest registry is
`lib/documents/pdf/src/reviewed_pdf_fixture_digests.dart`. It is immutable program
configuration, with no enrollment API, setting, serialized claim or picker action
that can add a digest. Selection never edits this corpus or registry.

The 40 marked cases come from the independently approved Correction 1 generator
`test/support/pdf_geometry_checks.dart`: ten geometry cases at four rotations.
Every content stream contains only the two controlled red/blue rectangles.
Disjoint cases are deliberately admitted negative controls that the geometry
reader rejects. Four blank PDF controls correspond to the existing adapter
rotation, page-limit and workflow regressions. `truncated-controlled.pdf` is an
explicitly truncated local ASCII negative control for fixed corruption outcomes.
There are no external PDFs, fonts, images, attachments, scripts or forms.

Each manifest entry records its file name, byte count and SHA-256. Admission
compares the exact immutable captured bytes against the compiled registry. The
largest member is 605 bytes. Verification tests compare every retained fixture
with its recorded identity and check a one-byte modification is quarantined.
The original marked geometry generator continues to produce identical admitted
bytes, verified by native and Web rendering regressions.

A SHA-256 match is an identity check against this controlled corpus, not a claim
that arbitrary PDF input or the parser is safe. Adding/replacing fixtures needs
separate source review of both the fixture bytes and the compiled digest entry.
No automatic enrollment or allowlist-writing utility is part of the project.
